clue.text: Take part and advance, having boxed favourite

indicators.note: to have boxed something is to have shut it inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: to advance towards someone is to come
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: A boxer joins the fight and moves forward, having already beaten the favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxed' suggests a fight, but here it only means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to enter a contest or race as one of the participants.

clue.text: Admit company head has accepted fine

indicators.note: something that has accepted a thing has taken it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbours like Dungeness
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A firm's boss owns up to having agreed to pay a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company head' reads as the boss, but the two words split: head is a headland, as in Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess is to own up to a fault or acknowledge a wrongdoing as true.

clue.text: Ridiculing second century leader

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a king leads his country

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a ruler from the second century.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking and ridiculing both mean making fun of someone with scornful laughter.

clue.text: The First Lady books social gathering

blocks.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: The President's wife reserves a party venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The First Lady' suggests the US President's wife, but here she is the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an organised occasion such as a party or reception where people meet.

clue.text: Key lease isn’t altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters before it are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A tenancy agreement that hasn't been changed is the important thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Key used as an adjective means vital or of central importance, the same as essential.

clue.text: Liberal ignores friendly labourer

indicators.note: whatever is ignored is left out, so that letter drops from the word

blocks.note: a friendly person is pleasant
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician snubs an amiable farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L out of PLEASANT to leave PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor farm worker or smallholder who toils on the land.

clue.text: Bit of quiet on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word counts by how it sounds

blocks.note: peace is quiet, and it sounds the same as a word for a part

explanation.surface: A short spell of silence during a radio broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a part or fragment of something, just as a bit is.

clue.text: Opinions of statute I’d revised

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone shares their views on a law they have amended.
explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are settled ways of thinking or feeling about something, much like views.

clue.text: Upset, face endless anger with mother country

indicators.note: endless means without its ends, so only the inner letters stay
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the order runs the other way

blocks.note: the inner letters of face
ire is anger
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Annoyed, a person confronts boundless rage alongside their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: AC + IRE + MA makes ACIREMA, which read upwards gives AMERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a nation, commonly the name used for the United States.

clue.text: In that respect, scoffing at drama

indicators.note: scoffing means eating greedily, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: as in 'there you have a point'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone mocking a play, at least in one particular regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' looks like mockery but is the British slang for eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre is the art form of plays and performance, a common synonym for drama.

clue.text: Core group of students bored by cryptic clue

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or mysterious, so the letters after it are jumbled
something bored through gets something drilled into its middle

blocks.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK
the fodder for the jumble

explanation.surface: A central band of undergraduates finds a crossword clue tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bored' looks like weariness but means drilled into.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central part around which other things gather, the same as a core.

clue.text: Next R.E.M. EP somewhat radical

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the run of words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across these words, ignoring the full stops

explanation.surface: R.E.M.'s forthcoming short record is a bit on the edgy side.
explanation.walkthrough: R.E.M. is an American rock band and an EP is a short record.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and radical both describe views or measures far from the moderate centre.

clue.text: Being sixteen badly inhibits Conservative backing European

indicators.note: badly suggests done wrongly, so the word before it is scrambled
backing here means standing at the back, so that letter comes last
to inhibit is to hold in or restrain, so the letter is held inside

blocks.note: the fodder for the jumble
E is the abbreviation for European
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old's poor behaviour holds back a Tory who supports Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled SIXTEEN with E at its back makes EXISTENE, which then holds C before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun means the state of existing or living, which is existence.

clue.text: Surprise romantic meeting discussed by Jonathan Ross?

indicators.note: Jonathan Ross is a British TV presenter famous for saying his Rs as Ws, so the word is said in his voice

blocks.note: a romantic meeting is a tryst, which with the R said as W sounds like this word

explanation.surface: A chat show host reveals an unexpected secret date.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonathan Ross has a well-known rhotacism, so his 'tryst' comes out as 'twist'; the question mark flags the liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is an unexpected turn in a story, a surprise development.

clue.text: Sweeten sauces from the East

indicators.note: in an across answer, coming from the east means reading from right to left

blocks.note: ragus are Italian meat sauces

explanation.surface: Adding sweetness to oriental sauces.
explanation.definitionFit: To sugar something is to add sweetening to it, as one sugars tea.

clue.text: Prompting buzz about artist, excited at last

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the others
at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: to give someone a buzz is to give them a ring on the phone
Tracey Emin is a British artist
the last letter of excited

explanation.surface: A phone call about an artist prompts excitement at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a favourite crossword artist, famous for her unmade bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminding someone means prompting them to remember something they might forget.

clue.text: Direct the setter’s friend to cover Hendrix periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
to cover something is to go around it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the setter is me, so the setter's is I'm
a mate is a friend
the second, fourth and sixth letters of Hendrix

explanation.surface: A setter's friend is asked to stand in for Jimi Hendrix now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a band playing a Hendrix song, but it means wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate and direct both describe something with nothing in between, as in a direct or immediate cause.

clue.text: Dim nieces misused drugs

indicators.note: misused means wrongly handled, so the letters before it come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Not-so-bright young relatives abused narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicines are drugs taken to treat illness, the pharmaceutical sense of the word.

clue.text: Confused, Charlie walked after son

indicators.note: after places those pieces behind the one named next

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ramble is to walk for pleasure in the country

explanation.surface: A bewildered man named Charlie strolled behind his boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrambled describes muddled thinking or jumbled order, a sense shared with confused.

clue.text: Barely used fast rides in resort

indicators.note: barely suggests stripped bare, so each word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: inner letters
inner letters
inner letters

explanation.surface: Thrill rides at a holiday town that hardly anyone uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town is a coastal holiday spot, and a resort is a place people visit for leisure.

clue.text: Understand Grealish has snubbed sides before introduction to Everton

indicators.note: snubbing the sides means cutting off the first and last letters
an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: Jack Grealish is an England footballer; drop his surname's outside letters
the opening letter of Everton, an English football club

explanation.surface: A footballer ignores the wings before joining a Merseyside club.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Premier League club in Liverpool, a likely transfer for an England winger.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or comprehend it, the same as understand.

clue.text: Great drink with former monarch

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: Having a fine drink with a one-time king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise meaning excellent or wonderful, a synonym for great.

clue.text: Supply extremely poor poet with ecstasy

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outer letters of the word

blocks.note: the outer letters of poor
Ovid was a Roman poet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone provides a destitute poet with a party drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide is to make something available or furnish it, which is to supply it.

clue.text: Quits or extends contract?

blocks.note: first meaning: gives up a job
second meaning: signs again, as a footballer staying at the club

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second meaning needs a hyphen: re-signs, signs again.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way the word means leaves a post; read with a hyphen it means signs a fresh deal.

clue.text: A profit once more

blocks.note: taken as written
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Making money for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Again means another time or repeated, the same as once more.

clue.text: Causes old clubs and casinos to change

indicators.note: to change means to be altered, so the word before it is reordered

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
the fodder for the jumble

explanation.surface: Vintage nightclubs and gambling dens bring about transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: To occasion something is to bring it about, so occasions works as a verb meaning causes.

clue.text: Topless dirty drunk

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, so topless drops it

blocks.note: something dirty is soiled

explanation.surface: A shirtless, grubby person who has had too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, as in well oiled.

clue.text: Small bird back at sea

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A little seabird returns over the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship or boat, its back end on the water.

clue.text: First home – is this all regularly missing?

indicators.note: missing at regular intervals means every other letter drops out

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Someone at their first house asks whether this is everything that's gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means coming at the beginning, the same as first.

clue.text: Requiring massaging, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said by others, so the word goes by its spoken form

blocks.note: kneading is massaging, as with dough or muscles; the K is silent

explanation.surface: Apparently in want of a good rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Needing and requiring both mean lacking something that must be had.

clue.text: Came out with revolutionary qualification including maths, primarily

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning over, so the word is read backwards
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter counts
including means taking inside, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a degree is a university qualification
the first letter of maths

explanation.surface: A graduate emerged with a radical maths degree.
explanation.walkthrough: DEGREE reversed is EERGED, which takes in M after its first E: E-M-ERGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out from somewhere into view.

clue.text: Vocalists in Germany aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on the ship, so those pieces go inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
GER is the abbreviation for Germany
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Performers on a cruise in German waters.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and GER go aboard SS: S-INGER-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Singers are people who use their voice to perform songs, i.e. vocalists.
